content: Tauri 2 is a good shell choice for this product: its Rust backend can host native bridges, TAO owns cross-platform windows, WRY owns WebView rendering, and the frontend is framework agnostic. The global-shortcut plugin supports macOS and Windows but requires explicit capabilities. Keep overlay creation/hit testing/fullscreen/monitor and capture in Rust/native adapters; keep toolbar/settings UI in TypeScript. A native canvas/WebGL layer should render strokes; if WebView composition proves unreliable, retain an escape hatch for a platform-native view.
